title: Field Elm: Old Field Elms You Can Visit
meta_description: Wait for me under the elm is French for you will be waiting a while, and this is that elm. Three field elms mapped, in Paris, Vienna and Trento.
intro: French has a phrase for being kept waiting: attendez-moi sous l'orme, wait for me under the elm. The elm in question stood in front of the Saint-Gervais church in Paris, where debts were repaid on agreed days and judges heard disputes in the shade, and an elm has stood on that spot since the Middle Ages. The one there now was planted in 1935, after the Revolution felled its predecessor, allegedly for cannon carriages; the motif survives in the wrought iron balconies around the square, worked into the metal in the 1730s. Ulmus minor was the species Dutch elm disease hit hardest, which is why the other two matter. Vienna's was planted in 1915 on a green strip down the middle of a street. Trento's is 393 centimetres round and carries no age at all.
